why: A quarter dose fills the shared settle gate (already saturated at a=0.25), and that gate fixes only the moderate-length share of the 164->205 hard-set gap, so theta(0.25) recovers about a third of it.
Code-RL carries only the shared gate and none of the math-specific part, so on hard328 it gets the same partial gain as theta(0.25), well short of RL's 205.
theta(0.5) has the saturated shared gate plus about half of the math-specific part, which builds up with dose, so it falls between theta(0.25) (~176) and RL (~205).
With only the shared gate, Code-RL reaches about 177 against RL plain's 206 on hard328, a deficit of about 9 points.
theta(0.5) has only about half the math-specific part, so it stays about 21 problems (6 points) below RL plain's 206.
Both have the shared gate, but only theta(0.5) has some of the math-specific part, so Code-RL comes out slightly behind it.
Any outcome-reward RL difference learns the low-dose shared gate, and MATH-500 with the cue mostly measures that gate, so the 3.0 Math-RL lands near the 3.1 cue plateau of 441-457.
RL-Zero-Mix is outcome-reward RL, so it learns the same saturating gate and reaches the MATH-500 cue plateau.
Even general-domain outcome-reward RL learns the shared settle gate (Code-RL does, through orthogonal weights), so it gets most of the plateau gain over the 410 base cue.
The 3.0 Code-RL learns the shared gate just as 3.1 Code-RL did (450 with the cue), so it scores near the plateau once the cue fixes the format.
IF-RL is outcome-reward RL on the same base, so it gates the same settle-verify-stop behaviour and gets most of the MATH-500 cue gain.
